clue.text: Cunning in Bow

definitions.meaning: an adjective for knowingly sly, as in a smile that hints at a secret
a curved shape, like a bent bow or a bridge's span

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sly trick played in Bow, the East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bow look like the East London district, as if 'Cunning in Bow' were a local trait; it is just the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the adjective for playful slyness and the noun for a bow-shaped curve.

clue.text: Handles made by your own fair hand

definitions.text: Handles made by your own fair hand

parts.note: the surface pushes things you grip, on doors or cups; the setter means slang for names

parts.words: made by your own fair hand
parts.note: names written out in the owner's own handwriting, signatures

explanation.surface: Handles, as on doors or cups, apparently crafted by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handles' looks like the things you grip, but it is slang for names; a name signed in your own hand is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a handle is a name, and a signature is a name in its owner's handwriting.

clue.text: 'Plastic' attribute comedian carries

parts.note: to attribute a deed to someone is to give them the praise for it
a joker, a funny person: 'he's a real ___'

explanation.surface: A comedian carries some quality that is fake, 'plastic'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Plastic' flag it as slang for what you pay with, not the adjective for fake. 'Carries' is the link: the two pieces carry the definition, that is, together they amount to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday slang: 'plastic' means payment cards, as in 'can I pay with plastic?'

clue.text: Amphibian making up most of sausage with a half of beer

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter
a half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the back pair

parts.note: the spicy Italian sausage without its final I
and = with, together with
the back half of BEER

explanation.surface: A pub lunch: sausage and a half of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A half of beer' reads as a pub order, a half-pint; here it is literally half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain category: this lizard-like creature of damp places is an amphibian, like a newt.

clue.text: Champion — Pole — sat uneasily

indicators.note: someone sitting uneasily shifts about, so the letters do not stay put

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A Polish champion sat nervously, perhaps before a final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a champion of a cause, its advocate, not a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended sense: beyond Christ's twelve, the word means any zealous advocate of a cause.

clue.text: Not 'BBC' — nor 'YMCA' — in need of correction?

definitions.text: Not 'BBC' — nor 'YMCA' — in need of correction?

indicators.note: letters that need correcting are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A pedant insists BBC is not the right term, and nor is YMCA.
explanation.walkthrough: The pedant's point: the strict term covers abbreviations said as words (NATO), while BBC is read letter by letter, an initialism. So the whole clue describes the answer as well as spelling it.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: the pedant's rule that such a word is pronounced as a word, which BBC is not, makes the whole clue a definition.

clue.text: Responded to advice, ultimately wise: eschewed immaturity

parts.note: to respond to advice is to follow it through, two words

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the end letter of the word before

parts.note: last letter of ADVICE
a synonym for wise, as in counsel

explanation.surface: Someone heeds good advice and grows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' attaches to 'advice' before it, not 'wise' after it; wise supplies its synonym whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to behave as befits your years is to put childishness behind you.

clue.text: Redecorate beehive?

definitions.meaning: the phrasal verb for renovating a house
a beehive is a hairdo piled high on the head

explanation.surface: A beekeeper decides the hive needs redecorating.
explanation.walkthrough: The beehive is the tall 1960s hairstyle, not a home for bees; the question mark admits the stretch of reading the answer as 'a do, piled up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for renovate, and a pun: a hairdo worn up high.

clue.text: Skates, and beams

definitions.meaning: skates are flat, wing-finned sea fish

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to be about an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skates' looks like the verb or the boots; it is the flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates belong to the family of flat cartilaginous fish, and the same word means beams of light.

clue.text: Professorial material largely affectedly quaint

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so keep most of the word and drop its last letter

parts.note: the woollen cloth of the stereotyped professor's jacket, minus its final D

explanation.surface: A fusty academic's jacket fabric judged old-fashioned and precious.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon professor wears a tweed jacket with elbow patches; 'largely' drops the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means cutesy or quaint in a self-conscious way.

clue.text: Everyman? This means I'm about to say goodbye

definitions.meaning: Everyman is the setter's name, so the setter talking about himself: me

definitions.text: This means I'm about to say goodbye
definitions.meaning: the sign-off at the end of a letter, just before the name

explanation.surface: The setter hints he is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the name this puzzle's setter uses, and the answer is a jokey way of saying 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a humorous stand-in for 'I', which is what the setter is to himself, and the formal close to a letter.

clue.text: Fashionable, following some trend: snap!

parts.note: slang for stylish or cool
keen on, a follower of, as in 'she's ___ jazz'
the indefinite article: some, one
a craze: 'all the ___'

explanation.surface: A trendy shopper grabs the latest fashion: snap it up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like an instruction to place something after something; it is a piece itself. 'Snap' means lose your temper, not a photo or a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to snap is to lose your temper suddenly.

clue.text: Used a revolutionary means of capital reduction

definitions.text: Used a revolutionary means of capital reduction

parts.note: the surface suggests a radical policy; the setter means the machine of the French Revolution
capital sounds financial, but it is the head (Latin caput), and the reduction is its removal

explanation.surface: A radical government cuts the capital city's budget.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as economics, cutting capital or funds; 'capital' is the head, and the revolution is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: the French Revolution's blade reduced people by exactly one head.

clue.text: Pertaining to change that will get you a new coat

definitions.text: that will get you a new coat
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: the answer is what gets you a new coat

indicators.note: letters that change are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Advice on clothes: a change that earns you a new coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pertaining to' looks like a fixed phrase meaning 'about'; split it, and the letters of 'Pertaining' are what change.
explanation.definitionFit: Here coat means a layer of paint, not a garment, so the definition describes the act of painting again.

clue.text: Arboreal schema including many elders

parts.note: a diagram shaped like a tree, with branches
elder is a tree too, but here the elders are ancestors, grandparents and beyond

explanation.surface: A diagram of a wood full of elder trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Elder is also a tree, so the clue can pass for botany; the elders are one's forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogy chart branches like a tree, and its upper branches carry the older generations.

clue.text: A writer's credit

parts.note: used as is
a copyist or writer, often a journalist in jest

explanation.surface: A byline: the writer gets credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to credit someone with a work is to attribute it to them.

clue.text: Frenchman then knocked back drink for hero of democracy

indicators.note: a drink knocked back goes back the way it came, so write it backwards

parts.note: M. = Monsieur
and = then, next
ALE, a pint of beer, written backwards

explanation.surface: A Frenchman downs a drink to toast a champion of democracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads as drinking; it tells you to write the drink backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Nelson, South Africa's first democratically elected president.

clue.text: A little psycho rat I obtained for Danish friend

indicators.note: a little of the phrase is just part of it, a run of letters inside

parts.note: starts in the last two letters of 'psycho' and ends at the first of 'obtained'

explanation.surface: Someone gets a pet rat for a Danish friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Danish friend is Hamlet's: the Prince of Denmark's loyal companion in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Hamlet's closest friend at the Danish court.

clue.text: Couplet developed — needing three more?

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A poet's two-line couplet, grown, still wants more lines.
explanation.walkthrough: A couplet is a pair of lines; add three more couplets and you have eight, so the question mark flags a sum: two plus three twos makes eightfold.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: a couplet plus three more couplets makes eight, and eightfold is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: I'm bats about devouring a kind of rice

indicators.note: about means around, in no fixed order, so the letters are shuffled
letters that devour something close round it, taking it inside

parts.note: the six letters of I'M BATS rearranged, then parted after the fourth to take the A
swallowed by the shuffled letters, after the fourth

explanation.surface: Someone crazy about eating a particular rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm bats about' reads as 'I'm crazy about'; split it, and I'M BATS is the fodder, 'about' shuffles it, and 'devouring' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the fragrant long-grain rice of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Not one most sought after by media bubble

definitions.text: Not one most sought after by media
definitions.meaning: not an A-list celebrity, so the grade below
a raised pocket on skin or paint

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity is ignored by the press bubble.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as B-LISTER: a second-rank celebrity, not an A-lister. 'Media bubble' is a false phrase; bubble stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pun on the second-rank celebrity list, and a pocket of fluid under the skin.

clue.text: Disturbed, angry insect's nature prone to biting

indicators.note: disturbed things are knocked out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A disturbed wasp is inclined to bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining fodder to definition; biting is the sharp, cutting quality of a remark or taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: biting means sharp or harsh, as a critic's tone or a lemon's taste.

clue.text: Baby's here, rising to spoil quiet

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a synonym for spoil or blemish
p = piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: The baby arrives and wrecks the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces read upwards give the answer. 'Baby's here' is a definition by location: where the baby is.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by location: the pushchair is where the baby lies on a walk.

clue.text: A spot of decadence in Arabian seaport

indicators.note: a spot of something is a small amount of it, a few letters from inside

parts.note: letters four to seven of 'decadence'

explanation.surface: A little decadence in an Arabian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spot of' reads as a small helping of decadence; it asks for a run of letters from inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the port city of southern Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Yorkshire cats and dogs getting VIP treatment

parts.note: a seaside town in North Yorkshire
cats and dogs are household animals

explanation.surface: Pampered Yorkshire cats and dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire' stands for a place in it: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire. 'Cats and dogs' may prompt rain; they are just animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: rolling out the carpet of that colour is how VIPs are welcomed.

clue.text: Ancient Greek instrument can be heard? Don't trust me

indicators.note: what can be heard is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: LYRE, the small Greek harp, which said aloud sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A lyre-player speaks, then warns you not to trust him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the answer's voice: 'don't trust me' is what the untrustworthy person would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition in the first person: the clue speaks as the untruthful person would, warning you off.

clue.text: Mentor, gone bananas, somewhere on the Adriatic

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A mentor has lost his mind on a Balkan holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone bananas' reads as one phrase for crazy; 'gone' is fodder and 'bananas' alone is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the small Balkan country with a coastline on the Adriatic Sea.

clue.text: Offensively gaze, lecherously eyeing, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A description of leering at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells and describes the answer: the initials give the letters, and the words say what the act is.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: the four words together describe a lecherous stare, which the initials also spell.
